name: Learn basic hand-drumming rhythms
blurb: Djembe, cajón, conga or a cardboard box — three tones and a handful of patterns will get you playing with other people almost immediately.
gear: A djembe, cajón or hand drum
steps: Learn the three basic tones: bass in the centre, open tone at the rim, slap at the edge with relaxed fingers.
Practise each tone until it sounds the same every time — consistency before patterns.
Learn a simple 4/4 pattern alternating bass and tone, hands strictly alternating.
Learn a traditional pattern with a clear call and response, and practise the call as a cue.
Play with a metronome, then with a recording, then with another person.
Learn to hold a groove for five minutes without speeding up.
tips: Slaps hurt when you tense up. The hand should be relaxed and bounce off the skin.
Volume comes from the rebound, not from force.
proof: You hold a pattern for five unbroken minutes at a steady tempo with three distinct tones.
